stories.title: Figure releases Helix 2.5 - zero-shot whole-body work across 30 unseen Bay Area homes, no fine-tuning (~56% task success)
stories.summary: Figure released Helix 2.5: robots deployed zero-shot into 30 previously unseen rental homes and performed whole-body household work (bed making, towel folding, toy tidying) with no data collection, fine-tuning or adaptation in those environments or objects - Index-pretrained policies completed 237 of 420 trials (~56%), up from a 9% baseline. For builders tracking generalization this is the first zero-shot, whole-body, 30-home-scale demonstration on a humanoid (Figure's claim) - the signal is that the pretraining corpus, not per-home adaptation, is doing the work. Caveat: it is a company demo in rented homes, not an independent third-party eval or a commercial home-robot ship date; the three behaviors were still trained with demonstrations collected elsewhere.

stories.title: SEC issues "Innovation Exemption" to de-risk tokenized NMS stock trading on permissioned venues - 5-year sunset, comment requested
stories.summary: The SEC (press release 2026-90, via official @SECGov) granted temporary, conditional exemptive relief so Tokenized Securities Venues are not treated as "exchanges" under the Exchange Act when trading tokenized non-market-standard (NMS) stock via permissioned AMMs and liquidity pools, with volume/listing caps, permissioned access, a 30-day issuer veto, and a 5-year sunset. For builders on institutional token rails this is the on-the-record regulatory opening that lets off-exchange, AMM-style tokenized-stock markets operate under the sandbox rather than the exchange regime - the same permissioned-venue pattern that Reg Crypto Assets and the tokenized-deposit work have been steering toward. Caveat: it is a conditional, comment-requested staff order for tokenized NMS stocks (not BTC), and the relief is sunsetting in five years unless converted.

stories.title: CFTC Market Participants Division no-action: passive software providers can route orders to registered derivatives venues without IB/AP registration
stories.summary: The CFTC's Market Participants Division issued a staff no-action position (Letter 26-25 / release 9300-26, 17 Sep) under which it will not recommend enforcement against providers of 'passive' software - and their relevant personnel - for failing to register as introducing brokers or associated persons, so long as the software only displays data and submits orders to CFTC-registered FCMs/IBs/DCMs, with no custody and no order discretion, including for event and perpetual contracts. For builders of wallet/app rails into regulated perps and prediction markets this extends the March Phantom-only relief to a broader 'dumb pipe' class. Caveat: it is a staff no-action, not a Commission rule - the relief is conditional on the software staying firmly in the passive category, and no separate article URL shipped with the @CoinDesk post.

stories.title: Insilico's Cell cover study releases LongevityBench + open Longevity-LLMs - 17-task aging-biology benchmark; L-Qwen3.5-9B tops the leaderboard
stories.summary: A Cell cover study from Insilico Medicine opens up LongevityBench - a 17-task benchmark spanning five biodata domains (clinical, genetics, epigenetics, transcriptomics, proteomics) - together with Longevity-LLMs, a family of compact open-source language models trained on clinical and multi-omics aging data, with models and data at longevitybenchmarks.org. The authors report that no single model dominated all tasks, that results shifted with question phrasing, and that omics-based age prediction remained the hardest task for frontier models; their compact L-Qwen3.5-9B claims top scores on the bench. For builders on the AI-for-aging track this is the reference public benchmark + open weights to test (and beat) aging-model reasoning. Caveat: it is an author-reported leaderboard on age/biomarker prediction, not a clinical longevity result - the models predict signatures, they don't extend lives.

stories.title: Geroscience framework: aging as 'loss of biological self-correction' - a unified lens for inflammaging and restored resilience
stories.summary: Bar-Or, Williams and Paredes published a geroscience framework in Geriatrics reframing aging as a loss of the body's biological self-correction capacity - tying inflammaging, metabolic drift and resilience loss to a single 'correction deficit' construct, and sketching how interventions (including metformin's TAME-style hypothesis) could restore it. For builders on the geroscience/therapeutics side this is a useful conceptual scaffold for prioritizing which 'correction' defects (vs which single biomarkers) an intervention should target. Caveat: it is a framework/position paper, not an experimental or clinical result - it proposes a unifying model and does not demonstrate that any specific intervention restores self-correction in humans.

quality.note: MDPI Geriatrics 11(5):134 (2026), 'Aging as Loss of Biological Self-Correction' - verified via live web search (mdpi.com returns 403 to bots; citation and title confirmed). Conceptual/framework paper; only a date is exposed, so noon UTC used as limitation.
